course.title: Art, Architecture and Society
course.description: Discover how different communities express their beliefs, identities, work and power through art and architecture. Explore real objects, paintings, homes, streets and heritage traditions in Southeast Asia and around the world, and learn how cultural ideas change and travel.

sections.title: Objects, making and power
sections.question: How do an object's form, materials and makers connect it to a society?
sections.description: Study a Japanese print, a Flemish painting, Javanese batik, Vietnamese and Chinese objects, art made for rulers in Egypt and Peru, and a Mughal court album, and see how making, work, exchange and patronage shape what people create.

sections.title: Buildings, belief and shared places
sections.question: How do buildings and landscapes express a community's beliefs, authority and everyday life?
sections.description: Explore Toraja houses, Borobudur, Angkor Wat, the trading streets of George Town and Amsterdam, and the Ifugao rice terraces, and see how people organise space around belief, power, work and the land.

sections.title: Stories, lives and public memory
sections.question: How do images and monuments tell stories, show work and shape what people remember?
sections.description: Read Thai Buddhist paintings, French pictures of rural work and a changing modern world, Rodin's monument to Calais, and two paintings of Prince Diponegoro's arrest, and ask who gets to picture history.

sections.title: Museums, heritage and connections
sections.question: How do museums, conservation and living traditions change what a work means?
sections.description: Follow Buddhist objects into museums, the Great Mosque of Djenné and the yearly work that keeps it standing, blue-and-white ceramics across Asia, and Mexico's Day of the Dead, then tell a fuller story about a work.
